title: Incidence and Outcomes of Human Adenovirus Infection and Disease in a Multicenter Cohort of Pediatric Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus (HAdV) among pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (allo-HCT) recipients can result in asymptomatic infection with risk for disease progression. There are limited data defining HAdV infection, disease, and case-fatality rates in a HAdV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) surveillance testing era. The current study aimed to define these outcomes using a priori definitions applied by a central review committee. METHODS: Pediatric allo-HCT recipients were followed up for 180 days after HCT at 10 pediatric institutions. Blood and stool specimens were collected 0-7 days prior to allo-HCT for serum HAdV immunoglobulin G and stool HAdV PCR testing. Clinical data, including HAdV PCR testing results, informed central review committee-designated outcomes of HAdV infection, including DNAemia, disease, and deaths (case-fatality rate). Outcomes were reported by HAdV surveillance testing status and by pretransplant research specimen results. RESULTS: The cohort included 819 allo-HCT recipients; 649 (79.2%) were under HAdV surveillance. The HAdV infection and DNAemia incidence among surveilled patients was 27.1% and 16.0%, respectively. The incidence of proven or probable HAdV disease was 10.9% for the cohort and, 12.6% for those under surveillance. The HAdV infection incidence was highest (13 of 25 [52.0%]) in patients with pre-HCT HAdV immunoglobulin G and stool PCR positivity. The attributable case-fatality rate for those with proven or probable disease was 13.5%. CONCLUSIONS: HAdV infection and disease are common among pediatric allo-HCT recipients. HAdV disease is associated with a substantial HAdV-attributable mortality rate. Clinical trials assessing novel HAdV in pediatric allo-HCT recipients are needed. Pretransplant serology and stool PCR testing could identify high-risk patients for trial enrollment.

title: A Virucidal And Endosomal Trapping Peptide Against Human Adenoviruses In Respiratory Organoids And Hamsters.
abstract: Abstract Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are common respiratory pathogens that cause severe, life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and children. Despite their medical importance, no clinically approved antiviral drugs exist. Here, we showed that 4H30, a 4-branched human defensin peptide, exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells with negligible cytotoxicity and a high barrier to viral resistance in A549 cells. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 4H30 exhibited a unique dual mechanism of action: direct virucidal activity through capsid disruption and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration. Notably, 4H30 remained effective against HAdV-3 in human respiratory organoids and against HAdV-2 and HAdV-5 in an immunosuppressed hamster model, significantly reducing viral replication and disease-associated pathology. These findings demonstrate that 4H30 can inhibit multiple HAdVs through a novel mechanism, offering a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections.

title: Efficacy of alcohol-based hand rubs against human adenovirus on contaminated hands.
abstract: Viruses significantly contribute to outbreaks in healthcare facilities, primarily through direct or indirect hand contact. Consequently, hand disinfection using hygienic hand rubs is a pivotal measure for preventing nosocomial virus infections in medical environments. In 2024, the EN 17430 standard was introduced as the first method to evaluate the virucidal efficacy of hand disinfectants under practical conditions. The new method offers an advantage over suspension tests (e.g., EN 14476) by enabling the assessment of hand rubs using human volunteers. This study aims to compare the results of these two methods by investigating the in vivo efficacy of various ethanol formulations and two commercially available alcohol mixtures against human adenovirus type 5 (AdV-5). The in vivo efficacy of pure Ethanol formulations in concentrations from 60% to 97% and two alcohol mixtures (M1: 45 % ethanol and 18 % 1-propanol; M2: 45% 2-propanol and 30% 1-propanol) were evaluated on the hands of 5 or 20 volunteers, utilizing a cross-over study design based on EN 17430. With the different ethanol formulations increasing reduction factors with higher alcohol concentrations were detected. Of the two alcohol-containing mixtures, only M1 demonstrated efficacy based on the requirements of EN 17430, the second formulation M2, however, narrowly failed effectiveness. In conclusion, results from suspension tests with AdV-5 were not directly transferable to those obtained with the alcohol formulations tested under practical conditions as per EN 17430.

title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.
abstract: Background In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Methods Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls. Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally. Results We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection. Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint. Conclusion Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.

title: Rare Adenoviral Vectored Vaccines for Emerging Influenza Threats
abstract: Background: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases pose a growing global threat, underscoring the need for vaccine platforms enabling rapid deployment and durable, broad protection. Although mRNA and viral vector vaccines transformed pandemic responses, limitations include waning immunity, restricted antigenic breadth, pre-existing vector immunity, and rare vector-associated adverse events. Here, we evaluate recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vectors for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. Methods: An H5 centralized consensus vaccine was designed using human sequences from the 2003–2006 bird flu outbreak and cloned into four low-prevalence recombinant adenoviruses. Mice received a single intramuscular or intranasal vaccination and were challenged two weeks later with high doses of diverse, lethal, reverse-genetics-derived H5N1 viruses. Immune correlates, survival, and protection from challenge-associated weight loss were assessed. Results: Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge against strains spanning twenty years of influenza evolution. Both vaccination routes conferred complete protection against antigenically related strains, and strong protection against more divergent clade 2.3.4.4b strains. Protection occurred before neutralizing antibodies could be detected, although strong H5 antibody responses were induced by all vaccines. Intramuscular vaccination generated strong serum IgG and antigen-specific T cell responses, while intranasal vaccination promoted robust antigen-specific mucosal IgA production. Conclusions: Adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 consensus hemagglutinin elicit rapid, broad protection against diverse H5 influenza viruses following a single intramuscular or intranasal immunization. These results support the continued development of low-seroprevalence adenoviral vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform for rapidly emerging influenza viruses.

source_body_en: Background: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases pose a growing global threat, underscoring the need for vaccine platforms enabling rapid deployment and durable, broad protection. Although mRNA and viral vector vaccines transformed pandemic responses, limitations include waning immunity, restricted antigenic breadth, pre-existing vector immunity, and rare vector-associated adverse events. Here, we evaluate recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vectors for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. Methods: An H5 centralized consensus vaccine was designed using human sequences from the 2003–2006 bird flu outbreak and cloned into four low-prevalence recombinant adenoviruses. Mice received a single intramuscular or intranasal vaccination and were challenged two weeks later with high doses of diverse, lethal, reverse-genetics-derived H5N1 viruses. Immune correlates, survival, and protection from challenge-associated weight loss were assessed. Results: Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge against strains spanning twenty years of influenza evolution. Both vaccination routes conferred complete protection against antigenically related strains, and strong protection against more divergent clade 2.3.4.4b strains. Protection occurred before neutralizing antibodies could be detected, although strong H5 antibody responses were induced by all vaccines. Intramuscular vaccination generated strong serum IgG and antigen-specific T cell responses, while intranasal vaccination promoted robust antigen-specific mucosal IgA production. Conclusions: Adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 consensus hemagglutinin elicit rapid, broad protection against diverse H5 influenza viruses following a single intramuscular or intranasal immunization. These results support the continued development of low-seroprevalence adenoviral vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform for rapidly emerging influenza viruses.

title: Adenovirus early proteins E1A and E3-19K reveal separable regulatory states of the ER stress sensor IRE1a.
abstract: The unfolded protein response (UPR) controls cellular homeostasis and viral infections. It is canonically initiated by dissociation of ER chaperone BiP/GRP78 from lumenal domains of transmembrane sensor proteins, including the central UPR sensor inositol-requiring enzyme 1 alpha (IRE1a). This results in IRE1a activation and splicing of X-box binding protein 1 (XBP1) mRNA, leading to transcriptional activation of XBP1 for cellular adaptation and sustained infection. Human adenovirus (AdV) preferentially activates the IRE1a-XBP1 pathway through the viral membrane protein E3-19K, yet the mechanisms underlying this selective activation remain unclear. Here, we show that AdV uses two distinct early proteins to dissociate BiP from IRE1a and activate IRE1a-mediated XBP1 splicing. The immediate early protein E1A forms a complex with the cytoplasmic domain of IRE1a, sufficient to dissociate BiP from IRE1a without inducing XBP1 splicing or UPR activation. In contrast, E3-19K is expressed downstream of E1A, associates with the lumenal domain of IRE1a, and induces XBP1 splicing without promoting BiP dissociation from IRE1a. Both proteins were detected in IRE1a-containing complexes, consistent with stepwise viral regulation. Together, our findings show that canonical IRE1a activation hallmarks can be mechanistically separated during viral infection, revealing distinct AdV-regulated IRE1a activation states with discrete upstream and downstream signaling outputs.

source_body_en: The unfolded protein response (UPR) controls cellular homeostasis and viral infections. It is canonically initiated by dissociation of ER chaperone BiP/GRP78 from lumenal domains of transmembrane sensor proteins, including the central UPR sensor inositol-requiring enzyme 1 alpha (IRE1a). This results in IRE1a activation and splicing of X-box binding protein 1 (XBP1) mRNA, leading to transcriptional activation of XBP1 for cellular adaptation and sustained infection. Human adenovirus (AdV) preferentially activates the IRE1a-XBP1 pathway through the viral membrane protein E3-19K, yet the mechanisms underlying this selective activation remain unclear. Here, we show that AdV uses two distinct early proteins to dissociate BiP from IRE1a and activate IRE1a-mediated XBP1 splicing. The immediate early protein E1A forms a complex with the cytoplasmic domain of IRE1a, sufficient to dissociate BiP from IRE1a without inducing XBP1 splicing or UPR activation. In contrast, E3-19K is expressed downstream of E1A, associates with the lumenal domain of IRE1a, and induces XBP1 splicing without promoting BiP dissociation from IRE1a. Both proteins were detected in IRE1a-containing complexes, consistent with stepwise viral regulation. Together, our findings show that canonical IRE1a activation hallmarks can be mechanistically separated during viral infection, revealing distinct AdV-regulated IRE1a activation states with discrete upstream and downstream signaling outputs.

title: An unusual case of adenovirus meningoencephalitis in an immunocompetent adolescent girl
abstract: Human adenoviruses can cause infections at any age, but most commonly involve the paediatric population. Adenoviruses may cause a wide spectrum of diseases depending on the infecting serotype. The various clinical entities include respiratory illnesses, conjunctivitis, gastroenteritis, myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, cystitis, and meningo-encephalitis. Here we present an uncommon case of the latter in an adolescent girl, diagnosed by cerebrospinal fluid RT-PCR. These include mild aseptic meningitis, subacute focal encephalitius, myelitis, Reye syndrome and potentially fatal acute necrotizing encephalopathy, but are all rare in an immunocompetent host.

title: Emergence of canine adenovirus infection in mink from five provinces in Northern China
abstract: Canine adenovirus 1 (CAV-1) is the causative agent of canine infectious hepatitis and fox encephalitis. However, epidemiological information regarding CAV-1 infection in mink remains limited. From September 2022 to February 2023, a total of 540 rectal swab samples from 18 mink farms from five provinces in China were collected, and viral nucleic acids were identified, sequenced, and analyzed. The overall positive rate across mink farms was 34.00%, with that of Shandong Province being the highest (67.33%). In Shandong Province, the positive rate of mink CAV-1 in Rizhao city was 100%. According to the fiber phylogenetic tree, the fiber sequences in the cities of Qinhuangdao (042803), Rizhao (042801), and Weihai (050101) were located in the same distinct branch and were different from strains isolated from other animals. These obtained fiber sequences were under purifying selection compared with the CAV-1 fiber (AC_000003.1). Compared with the fiber sequence AP_000069.1, the mutation of the 042402-TS amino acid changed the B-cell epitope and the 3D structure. However, the binding affinity between the obtained fiber sequence and the coxsackievirus and adenovirus receptor (CAR) was not different. These results indicate that strain 042402 exhibits notable genetic divergence in the fiber fragment compared with the strains from other host species, and the prevalence of CAV-1 has been confirmed in mink. Therefore, it is important to further clarify the evolution and molecular epidemiology of CAV-1 in mink in the future.

title: Four Recombinase-Aided Amplification Assays for the Rapid Detection of Fowl Adenovirus Serotype 4
abstract: Fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) infection leads to serious damage to the poultry industry worldwide. Accurate and prompt diagnosis is essential for effective management of FAdV-4 outbreaks. In this study, we first designed a pair of specific primers based on the ORF19A gene of FAdV-4 strain NP for recombinase-aided amplification (RAA) and optimized the reaction conditions. The results revealed that the optimal conditions for a sensitive RAA reaction were at 39 °C for 40 min. The minimum detection amount of FAdV-4 genomes was 10−2 ng/μL using RAA. In order to facilitate the result presentation of RAA, which was visualized using a lateral flow dipstick (LFD), and the optimal reaction time of RAA-LFD was shortened to 30 min. However, the minimum detectable amount of FAdV-4 genomes was 50 ng/μL, which was lower than the sensitivity of RAA. Furthermore, to enhance the sensitivity of RAA-LFD, we designed LbaCas12a-FAdV-4-crRNA and incorporated it into RAA to develop the RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD methods, respectively. Based on the RAA reaction of 40 min, RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD only need an additional 15 min. The minimum detectable amounts of RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD were 10−6 ng/μL and 10−5 ng/μL, respectively. These results indicate a significant improvement in the sensitivity of two detection methods. A total of 192 fecal samples from chicks were collected from Fujian province. These samples were then detected using these four RAA rapid detection methods. The results showed that 57 positive samples were screened by both RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD, which was 4 more positive samples than the RAA method and 14 more positive samples than the RAA-LFD method. Overall, we developed four accurate and rapid RAA assays of FAdV-4, which is feasible and of certain value in the application of FAdV-4 in clinical practice.

title: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting species B adenoviruses largely mimics the DSG2 receptor engagement mechanism
abstract: Species B human adenoviruses (B-HAdVs), including HAdV7, HAdV3, and the re-emerging HAdV55, cause severe respiratory disease and engage desmoglein-2 (DSG2) through their fiber knob. Here, we report the identification and structural characterization of two monoclonal antibodies, 5C5 and 6G7, raised against the HAdV7 fiber knob. Both antibodies neutralize HAdV7 and display cross-reactivity toward other B-HAdVs, with nanomolar affinities. Notably, 5C5 recognizes HAdV3 despite limited sequence conservation and exhibits greater neutralization potency than 6G7. Cryo-electron microscopy structures at 1.8 Å and 2.0 Å resolution for 6G7 and 5C5 respectively, reveal distinct binding modes: 6G7 engages the trimeric fiber knob at a 3:3 antibody: knob ratio, whereas 5C5 binds the apex at a 1:3 ratio. The 5C5 epitope overlaps with key DSG2-interacting residues, including a conserved pocket among B-HAdVs, providing a structural basis for its enhanced neutralization through receptor-binding blockade. These findings establish the fiber knob apex as a vulnerable site for antibody-mediated neutralization and identify 5C5 as a candidate targeting pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Vassal-Stermann et al. identified two monoclonal antibodies that neutralize HAdV7 and cross-react with pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Cryo-EM reveals that the potent antibody 5C5 blocks the conserved DSG2 receptor-binding site at the fiber knob apex, defining a vulnerable target for broad neutralization.

title: The evolving landscape of hybrid viral vector architectures: a persisting niche

source_records.title: The evolving landscape of hybrid viral vector architectures: a persisting niche

full_text: The development of hybrid viral vectors was historically driven by the need to overcome inherent limitations of individual viral platforms, including restricted payload capacity, narrow tropism, and limited control over genomic persistence. By integrating functional modules from diverse viral and non-viral systems, these chimeric constructs exploit complementary mechanisms to expand therapeutic potential. This review examines the architectural principles underlying hybrid vector design, framing their evolution as a logical extension of viral engineering strategies - such as pseudotyping and genetic chimerization - rather than as a retrospective response to the rise of non-viral delivery platforms. We highlight key structural configurations, including adenoviral, lentiviral, herpes simplex virus (HSV) amplicon, baculoviral, and bacteriophage-derived chimeras, as well as their integration with transposon systems (e.g., Sleeping Beauty) to enable enhanced persistence and increased cargo capacity. In parallel, we analyze the biological and technological trade-offs associated with increased structural complexity, including manufacturing constraints, cumulative immunogenicity, and regulatory challenges. Collectively, hybrid vector systems represent a modular and evolving design paradigm that complements advances in monoplatform vectors and remains a valuable approach for addressing complex therapeutic challenges, for example those requiring expanded capacity, multifunctionality, or combinatorial control of gene delivery outcomes. 4ConclusionDespite decades of development of viral and hybrid vector systems, their evolution remains constrained by fundamental biological and technological barriers arising from mismatches between optimal solutions for delivery, intracellular processing, and expression of genetic material. The concept of hybridization logically follows from the modular organization of viral functions, implying the possibility of redistributing them across different platforms. However, in practice, functional decomposition of viral systems rarely leads to linear improvements in performance, since the integration of heterologous modules is accompanied by epistatic interactions and disruption of coordination across vector life-cycle stages.Historically proposed complex multicomponent hybrid constructs have so far seen limited clinical translation, as indicated by the relatively small body of evidence for their clinical use, despite decades of development. Potential contributing factors include reduced efficiency associated with increasing complexity of multistep delivery systems, incompatibility between packaging and replication mechanisms of different viral platforms, and constraints related to cytotoxicity of individual components and the need for coordinated expression of multiple genetic modules. An additional limiting factor is the immunological burden arising from the combination of viral elements of different origins, which restricts both efficacy and the possibility of repeated administration.In parallel, optimized “monoplatform” systems have undergone substantial development, most prominently adeno-associated viral (AAV) and lentiviral vectors, as well as non-viral delivery platforms including lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and polymer-based carriers. Alternative gene delivery and expression systems, such as engineered AAV capsids with enhanced tropism and production properties, lentiviral vectors with modified integration specificity, and LNP platforms that have become central for mRNA and genome-editing delivery, have further expanded the available toolkit. In these systems, directed evolution of capsids, engineering of regulatory elements, and optimization of manufacturing processes have substantially expanded therapeutic potential without the need to adopt complex chimeric architectures. As a result, a significant fraction of tasks that previously motivated the development of hybrid constructs has been partially redirected toward improving existing platforms, leading to a shift of hybrid strategies toward specialized solutions aimed at overcoming specific functional limitations rather than achieving universal optimization of delivery.Nevertheless, monoplatform systems remain subject to intrinsic trade-offs regarding key parameters such as transduction efficiency, payload capacity, tissue specificity, immunogenicity, and duration of expression. While non-viral approaches have further strengthened this alternative trajectory due to their scalability and reduced immunogenicity, they still retain limitations related to extracellular and intracellular targeting, efficiency of endosomal escape, and the absence of native mechanisms for nuclear delivery or genomic integration. The persistence of these structural gaps between required functional stages of delivery underlies the continued relevance of hybrid systems, which are inherently designed to redistribute functions among initially poorly compatible yet functionally complementary biological modules, thereby enabling emergent properties that cannot be achieved within a single evolutionarily or technologically constrained platform (Table 2). full_text_sections.abstract: The development of hybrid viral vectors was historically driven by the need to overcome inherent limitations of individual viral platforms, including restricted payload capacity, narrow tropism, and limited control over genomic persistence. By integrating functional modules from diverse viral and non-viral systems, these chimeric constructs exploit complementary mechanisms to expand therapeutic potential. This review examines the architectural principles underlying hybrid vector design, framing their evolution as a logical extension of viral engineering strategies - such as pseudotyping and genetic chimerization - rather than as a retrospective response to the rise of non-viral delivery platforms. We highlight key structural configurations, including adenoviral, lentiviral, herpes simplex virus (HSV) amplicon, baculoviral, and bacteriophage-derived chimeras, as well as their integration with transposon systems (e.g., Sleeping Beauty) to enable enhanced persistence and increased cargo capacity. In parallel, we analyze the biological and technological trade-offs associated with increased structural complexity, including manufacturing constraints, cumulative immunogenicity, and regulatory challenges. Collectively, hybrid vector systems represent a modular and evolving design paradigm that complements advances in monoplatform vectors and remains a valuable approach for addressing complex therapeutic challenges, for example those requiring expanded capacity, multifunctionality, or combinatorial control of gene delivery outcomes.
full_text_sections.conclusion: 4ConclusionDespite decades of development of viral and hybrid vector systems, their evolution remains constrained by fundamental biological and technological barriers arising from mismatches between optimal solutions for delivery, intracellular processing, and expression of genetic material. The concept of hybridization logically follows from the modular organization of viral functions, implying the possibility of redistributing them across different platforms. However, in practice, functional decomposition of viral systems rarely leads to linear improvements in performance, since the integration of heterologous modules is accompanied by epistatic interactions and disruption of coordination across vector life-cycle stages.Historically proposed complex multicomponent hybrid constructs have so far seen limited clinical translation, as indicated by the relatively small body of evidence for their clinical use, despite decades of development. Potential contributing factors include reduced efficiency associated with increasing complexity of multistep delivery systems, incompatibility between packaging and replication mechanisms of different viral platforms, and constraints related to cytotoxicity of individual components and the need for coordinated expression of multiple genetic modules. An additional limiting factor is the immunological burden arising from the combination of viral elements of different origins, which restricts both efficacy and the possibility of repeated administration.In parallel, optimized “monoplatform” systems have undergone substantial development, most prominently adeno-associated viral (AAV) and lentiviral vectors, as well as non-viral delivery platforms including lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and polymer-based carriers. Alternative gene delivery and expression systems, such as engineered AAV capsids with enhanced tropism and production properties, lentiviral vectors with modified integration specificity, and LNP platforms that have become central for mRNA and genome-editing delivery, have further expanded the available toolkit. In these systems, directed evolution of capsids, engineering of regulatory elements, and optimization of manufacturing processes have substantially expanded therapeutic potential without the need to adopt complex chimeric architectures. As a result, a significant fraction of tasks that previously motivated the development of hybrid constructs has been partially redirected toward improving existing platforms, leading to a shift of hybrid strategies toward specialized solutions aimed at overcoming specific functional limitations rather than achieving universal optimization of delivery.Nevertheless, monoplatform systems remain subject to intrinsic trade-offs regarding key parameters such as transduction efficiency, payload capacity, tissue specificity, immunogenicity, and duration of expression. Each provided a distinct balance of efficiency and biological constraint. Adenoviral vectors (AdVV) enabled robust transient expression and efficient transduction of non-dividing cells but were associated with pronounced immunogenicity. γ-Retroviruses and lentiviruses supported stable genomic integration and long-term expression, yet raised concerns regarding insertional mutagenesis; γ-retroviruses additionally required cell division for efficient integration. AAV vectors demonstrated a comparatively favorable safety profile and durable expression in post-mitotic tissues but were limited by a restricted packaging capacity (∼4.7 kb), manufacturing challenges, and limited feasibility of re-administration due to neutralizing antibodies (Reiser, 2000; Lieber et al., 1999; Shayakhmetov et al., 2002; Hac et al., 2025; Nowicki et al., 2020; Yoder et al., 2021; Bestor, 2000; Pannell et al., 2000).By the 1990s, it had become evident that no single viral system simultaneously optimized delivery efficiency, safety, tropism, and genomic payload capacity. Within this context - well before the emergence of contemporary lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms - hybrid viral vectors (VV) began to appear as a logical extension of viral engineering. Pseudotyping of retroviral vectors with vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein (VSV-G) expanded tropism and enhanced particle stability (Duvergé and Negroni, 2020; Emi et al., 1991; Friedmann and Yee, 1995; Yu and Schaffer, 2006). Adeno–retroviral and adeno–AAV hybrid systems were explored to combine the high transduction efficiency of adenovirus with the integration or persistence properties of other vectors. In some cases, non-viral systems could also serve as donors of integration capability: for example, incorporation of transposon genomic elements (terminal repeats) can also yield hybrid vectors able to integrate genetic cargo into the host genome in the presence of transposase activity in target cells. Chimeric constructs incorporating packaging, regulatory, or capsid elements from different viral systems further illustrated an early strategy of functional complementation. Hybridization thus emerged as an intrinsic evolutionary step within viral vector development rather than as a response to non-viral technologies (Duvergé and Negroni, 2020; Lieber et al., 1999; Müther et al., 2009a; Feng et al., 1997; Caplen et al., 1999; Duisit et al., 1999; Kubo and Mitani, 2003; Kuate et al., 2004; Murphy et al., 2002; Tan et al., 1999; Soifer et al., 2001; Cunningham et al., 2024).In parallel, non-viral delivery platforms evolved substantially, including polymeric carriers and lipid nanoparticles. LNP systems, in particular, have demonstrated high transfection efficiency in vitro and have achieved clinical validation in the context of mRNA therapeutics and vaccination. Their advantages include cell-free manufacturing, compositional modularity, and scalable production processes. However, their biological limitations are systemic rather than purely technological. In vivo delivery largely depends on endocytic uptake with incomplete and variable endosomal escape; systemic administration often results in pronounced organ accumulation (notably hepatic enrichment for many LNP formulations); active nuclear import mechanisms for DNA cargo are absent; and expression is predominantly transient. In addition, repeated administration may provoke complement activation or adaptive immune responses (Bohana-Kashtan et al., 2004; Hou et al., 2021; Jung et al., 2022). As a result, a significant fraction of tasks that previously motivated the development of hybrid constructs has been partially redirected toward improving existing platforms, leading to a shift of hybrid strategies toward specialized solutions aimed at overcoming specific functional limitations rather than achieving universal optimization of delivery.Nevertheless, monoplatform systems remain subject to intrinsic trade-offs regarding key parameters such as transduction efficiency, payload capacity, tissue specificity, immunogenicity, and duration of expression. In vivo delivery largely depends on endocytic uptake with incomplete and variable endosomal escape; systemic administration often results in pronounced organ accumulation (notably hepatic enrichment for many LNP formulations); active nuclear import mechanisms for DNA cargo are absent; and expression is predominantly transient. The development of hybrid viral vectors was historically driven by the need to overcome inherent limitations of individual viral platforms, including restricted payload capacity, narrow tropism, and limited control over genomic persistence. By integrating functional modules from diverse viral and non-viral systems, these chimeric constructs exploit complementary mechanisms to expand therapeutic potential. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探讨混合病毒媒介系统的进化面临的挑战和限制,特别是阻碍其开发和应用的生物和技术障碍。背景强调需要克服单个病毒平台的局限性,例如有限的有效负载能力和对基因组持久性的有限控制。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对混合 媒介 设计的架构原理的回顾,重点关注这些系统的 进化 作为病毒工程策略的逻辑延伸,而不是对非病毒平台的响应。它分析了各种结构配置及其相关的权衡。
analysis_zh.methods: 该综述概述了不同病毒和非病毒系统的功能模块的整合,以扩大治疗潜力。它还讨论了结构复杂性增加的生物和技术权衡,包括制造限制、免疫原性和监管挑战。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该综述重点介绍了腺病毒、慢病毒、单纯疱疹病毒 (HSV) 扩增子、杆状病毒和噬菌体衍生嵌合体等关键结构配置,以及它们与转座子系统的整合。它还确定了潜在的限制因素,例如效率降低、包装和复制机制之间的不兼容以及免疫负担。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,混合 媒介 系统代表了一种模块化和不断发展的设计范式,补充了单一平台 媒介 的进步。他们指出,虽然这些系统具有潜力,但由于其复杂性带来的挑战,它们的临床转化受到限制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为正在进行的混合 媒介 系统的开发提供了信息,该系统是解决复杂治疗挑战的有价值的方法,例如需要扩大容量、多功能性或基因传递结果的组合控制的挑战。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认其局限性,例如随着复杂性的增加而降低效率、病毒平台之间的不兼容性以及免疫学限制。该证据基于对现有文献的回顾,被认为具有中等可信度。
